title: Snappy compressed data format
summary: Snappy is Google's fast compression format. The frame format: stream identifier (chunk type 0xFF, 'snappy' magic), then chunks. Each chunk: 1-byte type (0x00 compressed, 0x01 uncompressed, 0x02 padding, 0x80-0xFD reserved, 0xFE CRC32C, 0xFF stream identifier), 3-byte length, then data. Compressed chunks use a simple LZ77-like scheme with varint lengths.

structure.meaning: Type 0x00, 3-byte length, then: varint uncompressed length, then tagged literals/matches.
Type 0xFE, length 4, CRC32C of the uncompressed data (optional).
Tag 00 (2 bits): literal; length in 6 bits or varint; then literal bytes.
Tag 01 (offset < 2048, len 4-11), 10 (offset < 65536, len 1-64), 11 (offset any, len 1-64): back-reference.

notes: Snappy targets ~250 MB/s compression and ~500 MB/s decompression.
Snappy does not aim for maximum compression ratio; speed is the priority.
Used by LevelDB, RocksDB, Cassandra, Hadoop, and many databases.
The compressed format uses 2-bit tags: 00 = literal, 01 = copy with 1-byte offset, 10 = copy with 2-byte offset, 11 = copy with 4-byte offset.
